ingredients.name: Beetroot
ingredients.notes: peeled and cut into thin matchstick strips, about 3mm thick

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: add gradually as needed; reduce for a drier curry

ingredients.name: Lime or lemon
ingredients.notes: juiced; cuts through the beetroot's sweetness

steps.instruction: Peel the beetroot and slice into thin rounds about 3mm thick, then stack and cut into thin matchstick strips, sized as evenly as possible for even cooking.
Heat the coconut oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the fenugreek seeds and curry leaves.
Add the sliced onion and fry for 1-2 minutes until starting to soften. Add the garlic and green chillies and cook for another minute.
Add the beetroot strips, curry powder, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt. Mix well to coat the beetroot evenly in the spices.
Add the water, stir, and cook covered over medium heat for about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beetroot is nearly tender but still has a slight bite.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir gently and simmer uncovered for a further 5 minutes, until the gravy thickens slightly and the beetroot is fully tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice alongside a spicier meat, fish, or lentil curry to balance the beetroot's sweetness.

source_site: theflavorbender.com, cross-checked against hungrylankan.com and loveandotherspices.com for ratio and technique consistency
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 4+ independent sources with strong agreement on the thin-matchstick cut and coconut milk finish
notes: A beloved childhood comfort food for many Sri Lankans, often paired specifically with chicken curry and rice as a classic combination. The thin matchstick cut of the beetroot is considered important to the dish, as it allows quick, even cooking and the right texture; thicker pieces will need a longer simmer. The natural sweetness of the beetroot is balanced by lime or vinegar at the end -- some households use vinegar instead of lime for a sharper sourness. Beetroot stains plastic cutting boards and containers, so glass or wood is recommended for prep and storage.
